pattern.crimePattern: business partner cut out of a shared kiosk
pattern.notes: Fictional kiosk and fictional train times; Nairobi Railway Station is a setting only.

ob.reportedBy: Felix Wanyonyi, platform porter, Nairobi Railway Station
ob.text: Porter Felix Wanyonyi reports that Elijah Onyango (58), co-owner of the Stesheni Tea Kiosk on platform 2, was found dead in the kiosk storeroom at 18:50 during the evening rush.

people.name: Elijah Onyango
people.occupation: Co-owner, Stesheni Tea Kiosk; retired railway clerk
people.bio: Worked forty years for the railway, then opened a tea kiosk on the platform he used to clerk on.

image.brief: Kenyan man, late 50s, old railway-issue cardigan, flat cap, kind lined face, a tin teapot in hand, ID-photo framing

people.name: Dorcas Moraa
people.bio: Has run the kiosk with Elijah for five years and put in half the money. Takes the 18:10 to Embakasi every weekday.

image.brief: Kenyan woman, late 30s, short relaxed hair, apron over a cardigan, a commuter's handbag over her shoulder, guarded expression, ID-photo framing

people.name: Felix Wanyonyi
people.bio: Elijah accused him last month of stealing soda crates from the storeroom.

image.brief: Kenyan man, around 40, faded blue porter's overalls, a hand trolley beside him, wary, ID-photo framing

people.name: Kamal Shah
people.bio: Delivers to the kiosk every afternoon. Elijah owed him for three months.

image.brief: Kenyan-Asian man, around 50, short-sleeved shirt, delivery clipboard, reading glasses on a cord, tired and patient, ID-photo framing

people.name: Janet Achieng
people.bio: Sells commuter tickets at window 3 every evening.

people.name: Musa Ngala
people.bio: Has checked tickets on the Embakasi line for twenty years. Knows every regular.

people.name: Simon Wachira
people.bio: Shines shoes on a stool by the kiosk.

places.name: The platform-2 gate, then the 18:10 train

locations.name: Nairobi Railway Station, platform 2
locations.description: Evening rush. Commuters pour through the gates for the Embakasi and Syokimau trains. The Stesheni Tea Kiosk has a counter on the platform and a storeroom behind it with a door onto a service corridor. A schedule board hangs over the platform.

hotspots.label: Kiosk storeroom
hotspots.text: Elijah lies between stacks of soda crates. One crate of empties has split open beside him. The report says he was struck with it.

hotspots.label: Storeroom floor
hotspots.text: Under a crate, half trodden flat: a small cardboard commuter ticket.

hotspots.label: Schedule board
hotspots.text: A code-drawn timetable board. Tap a train row to see what it touches.

hotspots.label: Kiosk drawer
hotspots.text: The kiosk's trading licence in a plastic sleeve, and a folded note.

hotspots.label: Ticket window 3
hotspots.text: Janet Achieng has closed her window for ten minutes to talk.

hotspots.label: Shoe-shine stool
hotspots.text: Simon Wachira's stool and brushes, right beside the kiosk's service corridor.

image.brief: a platform at Nairobi's old railway station at dusk, commuters' blur, a small tea kiosk with a tin counter and soda crates stacked behind it, a painted train timetable board overhead, warm station lamps, no faces in focus
a small printed cardboard commuter rail ticket reading 'NAIROBI – EMBAKASI 18:10', unpunched, slightly crushed, on a concrete floor beside a soda crate

body.note: Inspectors punch every ticket on board between Nairobi and Makadara.

body.licence: Stesheni Tea Kiosk — licensee: E. Onyango
body.note: Buyer Tuesday. Tell D. Pay K. Shah after sale.

facts.text: Elijah Onyango was found dead in the kiosk storeroom on platform 2 at 18:50.
Elijah was struck with a crate of empty soda bottles.
A commuter ticket was under a crate on the storeroom floor: 18:10 to Embakasi, sold at window 3 at 17:52.
The ticket has no punch hole.
The 18:10 to Embakasi left at 18:12.
Inspectors punch every ticket on the train between Nairobi and Makadara.
The kiosk licence is in Elijah's name only.
Elijah's note: 'Buyer Tuesday. Tell D.'
Elijah's note: 'Pay K. Shah after sale.' He owed the supplier, Kamal Shah.
Janet: "Dorcas buys an 18:10 ticket every weekday. Today too, about ten to six."
Janet heard a crash of bottles from behind the kiosk at about 18:05 and thought someone had dropped a crate.
Janet sold tickets at window 3 without a break from 17:30 to 18:40 (her ticket numbers run in sequence).
Musa: Dorcas wasn't on the 18:10 today, though she rides it every day and always greets him.
Musa stood at the platform-2 gate checking tickets from 17:55 until the train left at 18:12.
Shoe-shiner: Dorcas went round to the storeroom door by the service corridor at about 18:00. He didn't see her come back to the platform.
Parcels log: Felix signed parcels in at 17:58, 18:04, 18:15 and 18:22.
Gate log: the Shah Bakery van left the station at 17:45.
Foreman: Kamal got back to the bakery in Industrial Area at 17:58 and did the stock count until 19:30.
Dorcas: "I bought my ticket and went home. I always go home on the 18:10."
Dorcas: "Elijah and I were partners. I'd never hurt him."
Dorcas says she put half the money into the kiosk five years ago.
Felix: Elijah accused him last month of stealing soda crates. He didn't.
Kamal: Elijah owed him for three months of bread and milk.

interrogations.intro: Felix keeps one hand on his trolley as if he might need to leave quickly. "I found him. Me. And he called me a thief last month."

topics.reply: He said I stole soda crates. I didn't. But I'm the one who found him, so you'll look at me. Look at the parcels book.
Dorcas runs that kiosk more than he did. She catches the 18:10 every day. Every day.

interrogations.intro: Janet slides her window shut. "I sell her the same ticket every day. I can tell you the exact minute."

topics.reply: Ten to six, 18:10 to Embakasi, like always. She looked upset. She usually jokes about the queue.
Mzee Elijah brought me tea at quarter to six. Then later I heard bottles crash, about five past. I thought he'd dropped a crate.

interrogations.intro: Musa comes off the 18:40 return train, clipping his punch to his belt. "Twenty years on this line. I know my regulars."

topics.reply: Mama Dorcas? Every day she greets me, 'Musa, how is your back?' Not today. Not on my train.
No hole. Then it was never on my train. I punch every ticket before Makadara. Every one.

interrogations.intro: Dorcas is found at home in Embakasi at 20:30. She came by matatu. "Elijah? I left him at the kiosk."

topics.reply: My name isn't on the licence because the county wanted one name. I put in half. Half! Five years.
I must have dropped it. I didn't take the train in the end. I took a matatu. I didn't feel like the crowd.

interrogations.intro: Kamal answers his phone at the bakery. "Elijah? He owed me, yes, but he always paid in the end."

topics.reply: Three months of bread and milk. He said he'd sell and pay me. I'm sorry for him. I'm sorry for my money too, honestly.

prosecutor.pass: Her ticket, on the storeroom floor, never punched. She never caught her train. That will hold.
fail: This doesn't hold up. Whose ticket is on that floor?
No. Ask the inspector what an unpunched ticket means.

proof.concludes: The ticket on the storeroom floor is the 18:10 ticket Dorcas bought at window 3 at 17:52.
It was never punched, so Dorcas never boarded the 18:10: she went to the storeroom at 18:00, and her ticket stayed on its floor.

eliminations.why: Felix signed parcels in at 17:58, 18:04, 18:15 and 18:22.
Kamal's van left at 17:45 and he was at his bakery from 17:58.
Janet sold tickets at window 3 without a break, in numbered sequence.
Musa was at the platform-2 gate checking tickets until his train left.

reconstruction.text: That afternoon Elijah tells Dorcas he's found a buyer, and that he'll sell her half too: the licence is in his name alone.
17:52. Dorcas buys her usual 18:10 ticket at window 3, like every weekday. Then, at 18:00, she goes round to the storeroom to argue.
About 18:05. She swings a crate of empties at him. In the struggle her ticket falls from her pocket under the crates.
18:12. The 18:10 leaves without her. Musa punches every ticket before Makadara; he never punches hers. She walks out to the road and takes a matatu home.

tier1.line: There's a ticket on that floor. A ticket tells you a train, a time and a window. Ask the window.

tier2.line: No punch hole, and inspectors punch every ticket on board. So whoever bought it never got on.
